text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.7% today as Brent crude oil topped $116 per barrel, a six-month high, driven by escalating Middle East tensions and fresh U.S. threats of military action against Iran. The company, as a major oil producer, benefits directly when crude prices rise—higher oil prices mean higher revenues and profits. The timing matches perfectly: news of Trump's threats against Iran and U.S. diplomatic pullbacks from Saudi Arabia hit markets yesterday and today, pushing the energy trade sharply higher.

This move fits into a much broader rally in energy stocks over the past two weeks—COP is up 12.6% in that span. Geopolitical risk in the Middle East has shifted the calculus for energy investors, who now see potential supply disruptions as likely enough to bid up oil prices and the companies that produce it. The added wrinkle of U.S.-Iran tensions also benefiting American LNG exporters shows how the conflict is reshaping which energy players win and lose.
